function: system (p. 7): a learned GNN (OAC-MPNN-Dif, OAC-MPRNN-Dif) sets pilot and data transmit power for over-the-air diffusion and aggregation in wireless FL (area 7), but every D2D link is single-antenna and there is no RIS.
notes: PDF matches: p. 1 holds the title 'Graph Neural Networks for Diffusion and Aggregation in Wireless Federated Learning' and DOI 10.1109/TMC.2026.3676512. Checks 1-5 pass. It is a research article with simulations. The learned GNN outputs transmit power (p. 9, Eq. 27; Algorithm 2: 'Ensure: The transmit power of UD'). The FL model is aggregated over the air (p. 3: 'the global aggregation is performed using the OAC scheme'), so the function is area 7 (p. 2: 'optimize the diffusion process and the aggregation process for WFL by using the wireless superposition property'). Trainer selection uses an auction and is not learned (p. 7). Check 6 fails. On p. 7, Eq. (15) gives the received signal ru = sqrt(pu) hu,u xu + sum sqrt(pu') hu',u xu' + nu, and Eq. (16) gives the SINR pu|hu,u'|^2 / (sum pu'|hu',u|^2 + sigma^2). Both use one scalar coefficient per link (Table I, p. 4: 'Channel coefficient between UD u and u''). On p. 11, Eq. (37) states 'ha and hb indicate the heights of the antennas transmitter and receiver', and the channel gain is |Gt|^2 = gl|gst|^2. Table II gives no antenna count, only 'Tx power gain of UD 2.5dBi' and a 2.4 GHz carrier. The BS uplink is never modeled with antennas. MIMO, RIS, and beamforming appear only in related work (p. 3), in the WMMSE-Dif baseline description (p. 12), and in the references. For the reviewer: if the OAC claim were judged nominal, the code would be function instead, because the D2D diffusion is a digital transfer (p. 7, Eq. 18: wkm = S/R). Either way the decision is exclude.
